artifacts.summary: 8-phase plan: 6 parallel EXTENSION.md trim phases with per-extension context-file migration and index entries, 1 phase making check-extension-docs.sh merge_targets.claudemd.source-authoritative and deleting both dead files, 1 final zero-Rule-U-advisory gate phase

memory_candidates.content: When a lint gate hardcodes a required filename (e.g. 'every extension must have EXTENSION.md'), and that filename is actually consumed only via a manifest declaration (merge_targets.claudemd.source), the gate's authority is misplaced: it will demand and length-check files that no code path ever reads, producing 'dead conformance' work. The general fix is to make the gate read the manifest declaration that determines consumption, and require/check the file only for extensions whose manifest names it. Two guards make this safe rather than a silent loosening: (1) emit an advisory (never a silent skip) when the manifest key is absent for a component that is NOT genuinely resource-only, so an accidental omission is distinguishable from an intentional design; (2) verify after the change that the gate still hard-fails for a component that DOES declare the file but is missing it, proving the gate was narrowed and not disabled. Structural evidence that a file is dead (no code path reads it) should be gathered before deciding to trim vs. delete -- trimming a dead file is the one strictly wrong outcome.
